title: Effect of a Narrative Educational Podcast on Stereotypes and Prejudice Among Medical Students
official: Learning to Improve Stereotypes Through Educational Narratives (LISTEN): A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
BACKGROUND Biases toward certain groups of patients (weight bias, ageism, racism, ableism and sexism) are common among health professionals and can affect the quality and equity of care. Traditional teaching formats such as lectures have difficulty engaging medical students on these deeply rooted attitudes. "Augusta's Oath" (original French title: "Le Serment d'Augusta") is a 16-episode narrative educational podcast (about 60 minutes per episode) produced by the Faculty of Health of Sorbonne University (Paris, France). Combining care stories, patient testimonies and insights from the humanities, it is used in an elective teaching unit to encourage reflection and change how future physicians approach patients. A previous uncontrolled study suggested that listening to the podcast prompted changes in perspective among medical students, but its specific effect on biases has never been tested in a controlled trial with validated measures.

OBJECTIVE To assess whether listening to targeted podcast episodes, combined with reflective writing, specifically reduces five types of bias: weight bias, ageism, racism, ableism and sexism.

METHODS This is a randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups, offered to medical students enrolled in the podcast teaching unit at Sorbonne University. About 500 students who agree to take part in the research are randomly assigned (1:1, balanced by sex and year of study) to one of two listening programmes of 8 episodes each (about 8 hours of listening), with a short written reflection after each episode.

* Group A listens to episodes on weight bias, racism and sexual and gender-based violence, plus control episodes that do not address the biases measured.
* Group B listens to episodes on disability and ageism, plus a different set of control episodes.

Each group therefore serves as the comparison group for the biases addressed only in the other group ("mirror" design). Participants commit not to listen to the other group's episodes until they have completed the study questionnaires.

At the end of the listening programme, participants complete attitude questionnaires once: AFA and ATOP (weight bias), ATIBI (recognition of implicit racial bias), AMMSA (acceptance of myths about sexual aggression), UCLA-GAS-F (attitudes toward older adults) and the revised ATPD (attitudes toward people with disabilities). Scores are compared between the two groups.

Participation in the research is voluntary and has no effect on course validation: students who decline follow the same teaching unit without any data collection. Data are pseudonymized, and participants who complete all questionnaires receive compensation for the time spent on research tasks.

EXPECTED RESULTS The investigators expect each group to show more favourable attitudes than the other group specifically on the biases addressed by its own episodes. Positive results would support the wider use of this narrative podcast as a teaching tool in other French-speaking medical schools.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Medical students in their 2nd to 6th year at the Faculty of Health, Sorbonne University
* Enrolled in the "Le Serment d'Augusta" teaching unit
* Informed consent to participate in the research

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refusal to participate in the research or objection to the use of their data (these students follow the same teaching unit without any data collection)
